units.spine: Hochhausen is ready for most troubles once and for none of them twice.

units.poolKey: Disasters & Famine: NO reserves, NO medical provision
units.spine: The town keeps no house for the sick and no food put by.
faces: A traveller says a man who takes ill here is nursed by whoever has room for him, because there is no house for the sick.
At the long table a woman says the town keeps no store, so a bad season is carried by whichever households had a good one.
The older heads here hold that the town has done without a store as long as they can remember, and they are the ones asked about it in a bad spring.
Asked at the church, the chapel's warden says the burying ground is the only thing the town keeps ready against a bad year.
The women who gut the catch say the town keeps nothing past a market day, the grain no better than the fish.

units.spine: The town is neither quiet nor in trouble, and which of the two it comes to is a matter of the next few seasons.

units.poolKey: First-Survey qualification (the reading is a first look)
units.spine: The town has been seen once and not lived in, and how safe it is has been taken from the one look.
Nothing organised is recognised here. A stranger who asks after such a thing gets a question in return and no answer.
Nothing at Hochhausen is run at another's word, and no interest here has a hand on the town's own business.
No wall stands here. Where the town ends is a matter of the last roof and the first field.
The town keeps no force of its own and keeps a charter hall. What the charter hall is asked for is not work for soldiers, and it is asked for often.
Nothing in the town is set against what it cannot see.
The grazing land and the last houses are in among one another, and nothing has been put up to tell them apart.
Everything the town eats comes up the road and none of it by water. Nothing is kept back here against a season when nothing comes.
